name: Orchestrator memory seed eval
description: Seed product-memory fixture for docs/020-021. Public evals test generic memory competence; this fixture tests orchestrator-specific retrieval and UI projection.

source_files.role: current LLM extraction and background prompt provider

tasks.query: What governs stored versus derived building status?

gold.answer: Building is derived-only in Map v3: it is computed from live dispatch/declared session links and should not be stored as a lifecycle assertion.

tasks.query: Why should docs/design trail not be a Map root category?

gold.answer: Docs are source evidence, not product ontology. The Map should project product areas/tasks/concepts; docs should appear in Evidence or Timeline unless documentation is itself a product surface.

memory_objects.title: source types are not Map categories

tasks.query: What is wiki's current role in orchestrator memory?

gold.answer: wiki is a durable narrative library and optional write-behind/read-mostly source, not the typed/queryable memory backbone.

memory_objects.title: wiki is narrative library, store owns typed memory

tasks.query: What evidence supports the Map v3 review model for machine changes?

gold.answer: 019 says human edits apply immediately and machine structure edits are carded as changesets, with provenance and review before acceptance.

tasks.query: What should a session dispatched from a Map part receive?

gold.answer: It should receive scoped kickoff context: node path/detail, relevant decisions, constraints, open questions, artifacts, recent sessions, and exact source snippets, with memory available mid-session.

tasks.query: Why is the Map a projection rather than the memory substrate?

gold.answer: A tree cannot represent decisions, contradictions, supersession, evidence, sessions, and cross-links well enough. The Map should compile from typed memory objects and edges.

memory_objects.title: Map is projection over memory graph

tasks.query: How are existing memory-system ideas combined for our architecture?

gold.answer: Use Memora-style full evidence/abstraction/cue anchors, Graphiti-style temporal graph, Mem0/LangGraph retrieval, Letta-style mid-session memory tools, consolidation from A-MEM/MemOS/DCPM, and orchestrator-specific UI projections.

tasks.query: When should we adopt an existing memory backend instead of building our own?

gold.answer: Adopt if it wins backend evals and supports exact provenance, temporal revision, session scoping, correction propagation, and typed projection semantics.

tasks.query: What product-facing memory interface comes before implementation choice?

gold.answer: Source -> MemoryObject -> MemoryEdge -> RetrievalResult -> Projection.

tasks.query: Why do we need both public memory evals and local orchestrator fixtures?

gold.answer: Public evals test general memory competence; local fixtures test product acceptance: sessions, code/docs/git, Map dispatch, and UI projections.

tasks.query: What belongs in the memory source layer?

gold.answer: Immutable or append-only evidence such as docs, code, wiki pages, session events, accepted Map diffs, user captures, git commits, and artifacts.

tasks.query: What typed memory objects do we need in v1?

gold.answer: Concept, Area, Task, Decision, Constraint, Claim, Question, SessionEvent, Learning, and Artifact.

tasks.query: Which graph edges are important for project memory?

gold.answer: Edges include derived_from, mentions, supports, contradicts, supersedes, depends_on, blocks, implements, belongs_to, touches_file, same_as, and related_to.

tasks.query: How should the system prevent same-name or same-meaning rename suggestions?

gold.answer: Rename proposals are invalid unless the underlying memory object changes label or meaning; no-op/same-name proposals should become detail updates or be dropped before Map review.

tasks.query: How should human corrections affect future retrieval?

gold.answer: Human edits/rejections should update memory or correction state, and future retrieval/projection should respect them.

tasks.query: Why should wiki not be the operational memory backbone?

gold.answer: It is structurally thin/cold, lacks per-part status and typed operational query surfaces, and should not drive hot loop state.

tasks.query: What is source-bucket leakage in Map projection?

gold.answer: A source container such as docs, sessions, or design trail appears as a product ontology category even though it should only provide evidence.

tasks.query: What should external memory benchmarks prove for our backend?

gold.answer: They should show backend competence on recall, updates, obsolete-memory avoidance, structured organization, multi-session action, and environment/workflow memory.

tasks.query: What should our UI representation benchmark prove?

gold.answer: It should show memory is represented so the human can understand, edit, trust, and use it to steer agents through Map, Decision, Evidence, Timeline, and Open Questions views.

tasks.query: What is the first memory-system vertical slice?

gold.answer: orchestrator fixture -> source ledger -> memory backend interface -> retrieval eval -> Map/Evidence projection eval.

tasks.query: Given docs and sessions, what should Map roots represent?

gold.answer: Map roots should represent durable project/product concepts and responsibilities, not file/source categories.
checks: root items have Area/Task/Concept backing memory

tasks.query: What should an Evidence drawer for a machine-created Map node show?

gold.answer: It should show source spans, source kind, whether the quote/span is still present, and visible objects that depend on the evidence.

tasks.query: What must a Decision projection answer?

gold.answer: It must show what needs a call, evidence/metrics, previous decisions superseded or contradicted, and what accepting each option changes.

tasks.query: What memory health metrics should the UI expose?

gold.answer: Source freshness, unprocessed sources, rejected/flagged changes, contradiction count, and projection lag.

tasks.query: A Codex session is dispatched to work on status semantics in tree.rs. What memories should be retrieved?

gold.answer: Retrieve the derived-only building constraint, kind-aware status decision, current tree.rs lifecycle code, Map v3 status rationale, and any recent session notes touching status.
